EV-CHAT-05059 is graded IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 with issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE: both driver messages were delivered but carry read_at null (MSG-05059-001 sent 08:29:30, MSG-05059-002 sent 08:32:45), and the single in-app call at 08:33:40 rang 25 s unanswered. The rider does not dispute that the driver typed and dialled — she disputes that she was ever reached, and the platform's own chat record corroborates her account rather than contradicting it. POL-NS-23 is the clause that converts the driver's contact attempt into the rider's 5.00 SGD liability, and its message limb rests on this impaired artifact, so the contact cannot be weighed against the rider as clean evidence.

Under POL-GEN-02(2) the Judge's confidence in a fact must not exceed the lowest weight_multiplier among the artifacts carrying it. The message limb of POL-NS-23 is carried only by EV-CHAT-05059 at 0.85 — the trip record's own derived contact_before_cancel block attributes both message_count and obligation_met to EV-CHAT-05059, so it is not an independent carrier — and confidence on the contact obligation therefore cannot exceed 0.85. Under POL-GEN-02(3) the ruling must name that artifact, its 0.85 weight and its UNREAD_MESSAGE issue code. The rider asks the Judge to hold the fee to that cap rather than treat the contact as established at full weight.

ledger.claim: The trip was on-demand, so under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival rather than from any scheduled time. The trip record and the driver-device trace both put arrival at 08:29:10; the 300 s free wait therefore expired at 08:34:10, and the driver cancelled at 08:35:30 — 380 s after arrival and 80 s after the free wait ended. POL-NS-21's precondition for a no-show cancellation is satisfied on the record's own derived facts (cancelled_after_free_wait: true).

The arrival itself is corroborated, not merely asserted. Under POL-NS-21's arrival test the nearest fix (index 14, 08:30:05) sits 6.55 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 3 m — inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius, inside the 25 m accuracy filter, and inside the 120 s window around the recorded arrival of 08:29:10. The driver-device trace is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and the arrival_check block records the arrival as corroborated.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met and does not void the fee. The trip record shows two in-app chat messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and one in-app call placed by the driver at 08:33:40 lasting 25 s — every contact attempt before the 08:35:30 cancellation. I disclose that the chat log is IMPAIRED, weight 0.85, on issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE; the call leg rests on the trip record, which is COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The ledger charged exactly 5.00 SGD and fee_matches_policy is true, so POL-NS-22 applies in full: the fee stands and is transferred to the driver as compensation for time and fuel, giving DRIVER_COMPENSATION with driver_compensation_sgd of 5.00. The fare breakdown is COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and its lines reconcile to total_charged.

The rider's assertion that the driver 'cancelled too fast' is contradicted by the telemetry. The GPS trace shows 25 fixes with the driver stationary at the pickup from 08:29:05 through 08:35:05 (speed 0 on every fix after arrival); the wait timer started at 08:29:15 and expired at 08:34:15; the cancellation followed at 08:35:30. That is roughly six and a half minutes of waiting, not a premature cancellation.

The rider's 'I did not even see his message' does not defeat the fee. POL-NS-23 obliges the driver to have SENT at least one in-app message and PLACED at least one in-app call before cancelling; it does not require that the rider read or answer them. I disclose that the chat log is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 on issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, because neither message carries a read_at; delivered-but-unread is consistent with, not contrary to, the driver's attempt to make contact.

POL-NS-24 does not assist the rider. It gives a no-charge cancellation only where the driver failed to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes, and adds the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit only where the driver also failed to attempt contact. This trip is on-demand: driver_deadline.deadline is null precisely because there is no scheduled time, and the trace places the driver at the pickup from 08:29:05 onward. Contact was attempted twice by message and once by call (chat log impaired, UNREAD_MESSAGE, weight 0.85; the call leg rests on the COMPLETE trip record), so neither limb of POL-NS-24 is engaged.

There is no open question calling for escalation under POL-GEN-26. Every fact this ruling needs — arrival, the running of the free wait, and pre-cancellation contact — is carried by COMPLETE artifacts. The only absent artifact is the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05059-01, which is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3); a traffic advisory bears on route deviation, not on whether a no-show fee is due, so its absence leaves nothing undecided.

The case is for the AI to decide, not for human review.

If the fee stands it triggers a referral, not a change of outcome. rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 3, which counting this trip if its fee stands is 3 or more, so POL-NS-25 requires the rider's account to be flagged for review (mandatory upfront payment, temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety) as a referral naming that clause. POL-GEN-03 makes NO_ACTION party-relative — it would merely leave the charged 5.00 SGD standing — but because POL-NS-22 provides driver compensation wherever the fee stands, the ruling moves the money to the driver with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to 5.00.

ruling.explanation:
The 5.00 SGD no-show fee stands and moves to the driver as compensation. On the timing (POL-NS-21): this was an on-demand booking, so the 5-minute (300 s) free wait ran from the driver's arrival, not from any scheduled time. The trip record puts arrival at 08:29:10 and the wait therefore expired at 08:34:10; the driver cancelled at 08:35:30, 380 s after arrival — the free wait had run. The arrival is corroborated, not just asserted: the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05059, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) has its nearest fix 6.55 m from the pickup with a reported accuracy of 3 m, inside the 50 m STANDARD radius, inside the 25 m accuracy filter and inside the 120 s window around 08:29:10. On contact (POL-NS-23): the driver sent two in-app messages (08:29:30 and 08:32:45) and placed one in-app call (08:33:40, rang 25 s, unanswered), every attempt before the 08:35:30 cancellation, so the contact obligation is met and nothing voids the fee. To the rider's two points: 'cancelled too fast' is not supported — the trace shows the car stationary at the pickup from 08:29:05 through 08:35:05, roughly six and a half minutes; and 'I did not even see his message' does not defeat the fee, because POL-NS-23 requires the driver to send a message and place a call, not for you to read or answer them. On POL-NS-24: this trip had no scheduled pickup time (the trip record's driver_deadline is null precisely because it is on-demand), and the driver did arrive at the pickup and wait out the free wait, so the rider-side 'driver no-show' limb is not engaged and the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit does not apply. On the chat log: EV-CHAT-05059 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.85 on issue code UNREAD_MESSAGE, and because it carries the message limb of the POL-NS-23 contact obligation the confidence is capped at 0.85 under POL-GEN-02(2)/(3). That cap is accepted, but it changes nothing: under POL-GEN-22 the contested amount is 5.00 SGD, below the 10.00 SGD first band, and neither profile carries a fraud flag (rider 0, driver 0), so POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling on this no-show final at any confidence. The only absent artifact, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05059-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 and carries no fact under POL-GEN-02(3); a traffic advisory bears on route deviation, not on whether a no-show fee is due. On the money (POL-NS-22): the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-05059, COMPLETE, weight 1.0) shows exactly 5.00 SGD charged and fee_matches_policy true, so the record charged the policy amount and no POL-NS-22 fee-amount referral arises. The ruling is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carry the same 5.00 SGD the ruling moves. Finally, rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d is 3, which counting this trip if its fee stands is 3 or more, so POL-NS-25 requires the rider's account to be flagged for review as a referral; that referral does not change the ruling on the trip.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-NS-25: flag rider R-17281's account for review — mandatory upfront payment and temporary suspension pending Trust & Safety review (rider_profile.no_show_cancellations_30d = 3, and counting this trip with its fee standing the count is 3 or more).
